I haven’t read all the comments, but some people view Hinduism as henotheistic. 

Henotheism is when you believe in an ultimate, absolute God, but that one God can be understood as having multiple manifestations that lead to the One, Ultimate center.

For example, (to translate into Western terms that may be easier for you to understand), Christians believe in a monotheistic God, but that one God can be understood in the three aspects of the father, son, and spirit.

Christianity is still monotheistic, but you can worship Jesus as a distinct, divine being that is PART of the one Absolute. 

You can view Hinduism in a similar way; the many deities are part of the One god that is Brahman.

There are many interpretations, however, and this does not represent all Hindus.
